title: Keyturn Host Protection Plan Schedule A: Earnings Share, Trip Fee Offset and Commercial Use
content:
## Schedule A

The plan a listing is written on under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan fixes three things about the money and the use of the vehicle: the share of the trip price the host keeps, the share of the marketplace trip fee credited back to the host, and whether the vehicle may be used commercially between trips. The ladder is priced so that the deeper the cover, the smaller the share of the trip price retained.

| Plan | Earnings share, percent | Trip fee offset, percent | Commercial use between trips |
|---|---|---|---|
| Keyturn Shield 90 Host Plan | 90 | 0 | no |
| Keyturn Shield 85 Host Plan | 85 | 0 | no |
| Keyturn Shield 80 Host Plan | 80 | 0 | no |
| Keyturn Shield 75 Host Plan | 75 | 2 | no |
| Keyturn Shield 70 Host Plan | 70 | 3 | yes |
| Keyturn Shield 60 Host Plan | 60 | 5 | yes |

### Reading the schedule

The earnings share column is the percentage of the trip price the host keeps under that plan; the remainder is the marketplace's. The trip fee offset column is the percentage of the marketplace trip fee credited back to the host; where it stands at 0 the plan carries no offset. The last column is a plain yes or no: commercial use between trips is permitted only on the Keyturn Shield 70 and Keyturn Shield 60 Host Plans.

### Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

On a hypothetical trip priced at 400, a host whose vehicle is written on the Keyturn Shield 85 Host Plan keeps 340 of that price, an earnings share of 85 percent; the same trip on the Keyturn Shield 60 Host Plan leaves the host 240, an earnings share of 60 percent. The figures are illustrative inputs and fix no price.
